project.name: Sample Classpath Matrix
project.description:
Proves that the stub runner's embedded WireMock actually starts and serves under every runtime we claim to support, rather than only resolving on paper.
This exists because of stubborn-sh/stubborn#142: WireMock's wiremock-jetty12 brings jetty-ee10 12.0.x, while Spring Boot 4.1 aligns Jetty core to 12.1.x and imports jetty-ee11-bom. Those load together and the stub server dies with
NoSuchMethodError: org.eclipse.jetty.util.component.Environment.ensure(String)
Pinning the core down to 12.0.x is NOT the fix - that is what broke spring-boot-starter-jetty applications in the first place. The fix is to align ee10 with the Jetty Boot already manages: 12.1.x publishes ee10 and wiremock-jetty12 runs on it perfectly well. boot-jetty below does that by hand for now, and from Stubborn 0.2.1 the BOM does it for you. sample-jetty-alignment lays the combinations out side by side.
The other way out is to stop sharing a Jetty at all - wiremock-standalone is shaded, carrying its Jetty relocated under wiremock.org.eclipse.jetty. It works, but the same shading relocates Handlebars, so Stubborn's response-template helpers cannot be registered against it. Prefer alignment unless you specifically want a stub server that nothing on the application classpath can perturb.
Each module below asserts both halves: the application's own Jetty is whatever its framework manages, AND a stub server boots and serves a request on the same JVM.
